title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 171 (General lien of bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys and policy-brokers)

content.overview: Section 171 provides that bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys of a High Court and policy-brokers may, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, retain, as a security for a general balance of account, any goods bailed to them; but no other persons have a right to retain, as a security for such balance, goods bailed to them, unless there is an express contract to that effect.
content.glance: Specified persons (bankers, factors, wharfingers, High Court attorneys, policy-brokers) have a general lien for the general balance of account, absent a contrary contract; others do not unless by express contract.
content.study: Bankers, factors, wharfingers, attorneys of a High Court and policy-brokers may, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, retain, as a security for a general balance of account, any goods bailed to them; but no other persons have a right to retain, as a security for such balance, goods bailed to them, unless there is an express contract to that effect.
